1.note: Here the **heart** represents the seat of a person’s emotions and will. David is saying that he will thank Yahweh with complete devotion. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with all of my being]

Here, **the gods** could refer to: (1) idols of other nations that the psalmist sees either within Israel or while traveling. Alternate translation: [idols of foreign gods] or (2) God’s heavenly council of angelic beings. Alternate translation: [the heavenly assembly]

2.note: David is using the possessive form to describe a **temple** that is characterized by God’s **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your holy temple]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you, the Holy One] or [all that is holy about you]

David is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is and to refer to his reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who you are]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **trustworthiness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [the way you are faithful to your covenant and for being trustworthy]

The terms **covenant faithfulness** and **trustworthiness** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [your complete reliability]

The phrase **for you have exalted above all of your name your word** is a translation of the written Hebrew text. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed some alternative readings, and you may want to follow one of those. The UST follows the first alternative. Alternate translation: [for you have exalted above all else your name and your word] or [for you have exalted above all names your word]
David is using the term **word** to represent what Yahweh has spoken. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all that you have spoken]

3.note: David is using the word **soul** to refer to his whole self. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **power**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be mighty]

4.note: David is saying **all the kings of the earth** as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be clearer in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [kings everywhere]

David is using **the words from your mouth** to represent everything that Yahweh has communicated. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the things you have declared]

5.note: David is speaking of what Yahweh does as if those actions were **ways** or paths that he walks along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [of what Yahweh does]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is very glorious]

6.note: David uses the word **Though** here to indicate a contrast between Yahweh’s supreme status and his attention to those who are humble. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Even though Yahweh is high, he still sees the lowly]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh’s supreme status as if it were a physical height, saying **Yahweh is high**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is supreme]

David is using the adjective **lowly** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [yet he sees lowly people]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh’s relationship to proud people as if it involved physical distance, saying he **knows** them **from far off**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the proud he keeps at a distance]

David is using the adjective **proud** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and those who are proud]

7.note: David uses the word **Though** here to indicate a contrast between the danger he faces and the protection Yahweh provides. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Despite that I walk in the middle of trouble, you will still keep me alive]

Here David is speaking of experiencing danger as if it were a place through which he walks, saying he will **walk in the middle of trouble**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I experience great trouble]

Here, **hand** represents Yahweh’s power to act. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you will use your power]

Here, **nose** represents the anger of David’s enemies. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the anger of my enemies]

Here, **right hand** represents Yahweh’s power to deliver. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will powerfully save me]

8.note: By **Yahweh will accomplish for my benefit**, the psalmist means that whatever Yahweh does will be to fulfill his purpose for David. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will accomplish his purpose for my benefit]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the way you are faithful to your covenant]

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please do not forsake the works of your hands]

Here, **the works of your hands** represents what Yahweh has made and accomplished. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [what you have made]
